$comment: VAPP-103: the input LIMITS every core enforces (the TS reference, the Rust core and through it Swift, Compose and gpui). An agent's input past a limit is refused with an issue, never worked on. `maxComponents` = nodes the reducer places in one surface's tree, template nodes included (the rest is dropped: `surface: more than N components; the rest is dropped`); a renderer's build holds at most `maxComponents` nodes too: the reduced tree's (after expansion, children and slots) plus, per template ITEM, its template subtree's (nested items charged when they are instantiated); the first item that does not fit and every later one are not rendered, with ONE issue on the template component (the same message). `maxDepth` = nesting levels of the REDUCED tree, after macro expansion (the root and every lifted template = 1, children and slots one level down; a Card, Section or Group macro adds a level; a deeper node is the Unknown placeholder, its subtree dropped: `nesting deeper than N levels`); 48 keeps every tree a core emits (2 JSON levels per node) inside serde_json's default recursion limit of 128, so reduced trees, fixtures and the FFI's JSON round-trip; the Rust core's recursive passes switch to a heap-allocated stack segment when the host thread runs low, so an iOS secondary thread's 512 KB never decides (a 48-level surface lays out on a 128 KB thread, debug build). `maxMessageBytes` = one server message as UTF-8 JSON (host routers refuse it: INVALID_MESSAGE). `maxTemplateItems` = template items one surface instantiates (beyond it the items are not rendered: `template: more than N items; the rest is not rendered`). `maxPointerBytes` / `maxPointerSegments` = a data pointer's length and token count (a longer write is refused). Generated into every target; src/limits.ts reads it.
